title: The Kindly House
premise: Folklorist Lior Winterbourne arrives in the isolated village of Hollowmere to record its songs, only to discover every tune ends mid-verse — a deliberate silence the villagers keep to avoid 'waking what listens.' When an excavation crew unearths a stone door sealed from the inside, the village's oldest families reveal a bargain: each generation must complete a ritual begun by the founders, feeding the house beneath the churchyard with memory, song, and eventually blood. Lior, a rationalist who refuses to believe, is chosen as this year's offering precisely because he is an outsider whose unbelief makes him 'clean.' As he falls for Mara, the sexton's daughter sworn to prepare him for sacrifice, Lior must choose between escaping alone and finishing the founders' ritual himself — sealing the door forever by giving the house what it truly wants: someone willing to stay. In the end, Lior completes the ritual not as a victim but as a keeper, and Mara chooses to remain beside him, both becoming the new founders of the kindly house.
about_author: Z. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist of regional folk music who spent years collecting songs in remote farming communities before turning to fiction. They write horror rooted in the belief that old places remember, and that every tradition exists for a reason no one wants to say aloud.

chapters.title: The Song That Stops
chapters.summary: Lior arrives in Hollowmere by late bus, recording equipment in hand. At the inn, an old woman sings a harvest lullaby that cuts off mid-line; when he asks why, she goes pale and leaves. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into unease as the first small wrongness takes hold.

chapters.title: Hollowmere's Silence
chapters.summary: Lior interviews villagers; everyone sings beautifully until the same verse, then stops as if struck mute. The vicar warns him gently that some songs are 'finished elsewhere.' POV: Lior. Emotional beat: mounting frustration and the first sense that the silence itself is a rule being obeyed.

chapters.title: The Sexton's Daughter
chapters.summary: Mara catches Lior poking around the churchyard at dusk and escorts him out, half-hostile, half-amused. She knows more than she says about which graves are never visited. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: wary attraction established against a backdrop of guarded secrets.

chapters.title: What the Crew Unearthed
chapters.summary: An archaeological crew digging near the churchyard strikes stone: a door, its bolts thrown from the inside. The foreman jokes about it; the village does not laugh. That night every dog in Hollowmere howls at once. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: dread arriving on schedule — something sealed wanted to stay sealed.

chapters.title: Records of the Founders
chapters.summary: In the parish archive Lior finds the founders' ledger: seven names, a covenant written in verse, and pages torn from 1743 onward. The missing verses match the unfinished song exactly. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the scholar's thrill curdling — his folklore is a manual, not a memory.

chapters.title: Mara Tells Him to Leave
chapters.summary: Mara finds Lior copying the ledger and begs him to catch the morning bus, revealing fragments: the house under the churchyard, the tithe, the harvest moon. He laughs it off; she looks at him like a marked man. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: love beginning as warning, duty pulling her two directions.

chapters.title: The First Verse Returns
chapters.summary: At the inn, the old woman finishes her lullaby for the first time in sixty years — and dies before the last note. The village gathers, silent, certain. Lior records nothing; his recorder has filled with static shaped like breathing. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: unbelief cracking along its fault lines.

chapters.title: The Choosing
chapters.summary: The oldest families convene in the vestry. Lior, eavesdropping, learns the excavation broke the seal early and the tithe must be paid before the harvest moon: an outsider, unbaptized by the village's fear, 'clean of belief.' His name is spoken aloud by all seven families. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: horror of complicity — she says nothing to save him.

chapters.title: A Door Sealed From Within
chapters.summary: Lior descends to the excavation site at night. Through the cracked seam of the door he hears singing — the completed song, in voices layered like sediment. He presses his ear to cold stone and something presses back. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: terror fused with terrible fascination.

chapters.title: Run, Then
chapters.summary: Lior tries to leave; the bus never comes, his car's engine flooded with dark water that smells of the churchyard. Roads loop back to Hollowmere. Mara finds him walking in circles and admits she tried once too, years ago, after her mother was taken. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: despair transmuting into intimacy — they are trapped together.

chapters.title: The Ritual of the Founders
chapters.summary: The vicar, breaking at last, shows Lior the full rite: seven verses sung at the door, each requiring a truth freely given, ending with a keeper who stays willingly. Refusal means the house takes what it wants, messily. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the bargain laid bare — survival has a price and it is named.

chapters.title: Songs the Village Refused Twice
chapters.summary: Lior works obsessively, reconstructing the missing verses from ledger fragments and the dead woman's final recording. Mara helps despite herself, teaching him harmonies her mother taught her. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: love deepening through shared forbidden work; loyalty to family warring with loyalty to him.

chapters.title: The House Below Dreams
chapters.summary: Dreams begin leaking upward: villagers sleepwalk toward the churchyard; children hum the finished song in their sleep. Lior dreams of a warm interior, hands, welcome. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: seduction — the house is kind, and that is the worst part.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Vestry Door
chapters.summary: The seven families move the ritual up, fearing the moon. Mara's father reveals she was meant to deliver Lior, and that her mother was the last keeper — still down there, still singing. Mara flees rather than confirm it. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: loyalty shattered between blood and love.

chapters.title: What Her Mother Left
chapters.summary: Lior finds Mara in the bell tower with her mother's journal: proof the last keeper went willingly, and that the ritual can be ended permanently if the keeper gives not just presence but a truth the house cannot digest. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: grief converted into resolve — there may be a way out for everyone.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Rises
chapters.summary: The village assembles at the excavation with lanterns and resignation. The door sweats warmth. Lior is led forward in borrowed clothes, anointed with grave-soil, while Mara watches, bound by her father's grip. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: calm fatalism — he has decided, and no one knows yet.

chapters.title: Seven Verses
chapters.summary: Lior begins the rite, giving each verse a truth: his unbelief, his loneliness, his love for Mara spoken before the whole village. With each verse the door opens wider, and the singing below grows joyful. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness braided — confession as weapon.

chapters.title: The Truth the House Cannot Digest
chapters.summary: For the final verse Lior offers the one thing the house cannot take: forgiveness — for the founders, for the village, for the thing below that only ever wanted to be remembered kindly. The house falters, hungry and confused. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: climax — compassion wielded as exorcism.

chapters.title: Keeper
chapters.summary: The door stands open onto warmth and waiting faces, her mother among them. Mara breaks free and steps to Lior's side, choosing to share the keeping. Together they speak the closing words; the door seals — this time from the outside, gently, like a hand closed in blessing. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved — she rewrites duty itself.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Dawn. The excavation is filled in; the crew remembers nothing worth writing down. Villagers finish their songs at last, weeping as the final verses come back to them. The vicar burns the ledger. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: exhausted relief shadowed by cost — some silences were mercy.

chapters.title: The Kindly House
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Lior writes to no one and records everything: the true song, complete, archived under a false name. Some nights the churchyard soil is warm underfoot, and the house below hums contentment instead of hunger. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace — survival achieved, innocence spent.

chapters.title: Two Voices, One Verse
chapters.summary: On the anniversary, Lior and Mara stand where the door was buried and sing the seventh verse together, adding a line of their own: a promise that whoever comes next will be met with kindness, not appetite. Far below, something learns the new harmony. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: resolution — the cycle broken, or perhaps finally made worthy of continuing.
